segments.text: 1. The present petition is an eviction petition filed on the grounds u/s 14 (1) (b) and (f) of Delhi Rent Control Act against the respondent in respect of one godown on the ground floor of the suit property bearing no. 2378­82, Chasma Building, Ballimaran, Delhi ­ 6.

2. Brief facts, as stated in the petition, are that the petitioner is the owner and landlady of the suit property and same has been let out to M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd. @ Rs.240/­ p.m. but M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd. is later on claimed to have been merged and was taken over by the present respondent bank and with this merger/acquisition the existence of M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd.

has been brought to an end which amounts to sub­letting, assigning or parting with the possession of the suit premises without the consent of the petitioner. It is stated that the suit property has been lying locked for the last about 14 years and due to its closure for a long time, substantial damage has been caused or permitted to have been caused to the suit property.

It is further stated that the suit property has been rendered collapsible any moment and is an alive danger for the other occupants of this property as well passers by and therefore immediate repairs to the premises is required which is not possible unless vacant possession thereof is handed over to the petitioner. It has been prayed that an eviction order may be passed in favour of the petitioner and against the respondent in respect of suit premises.

3. The respondent bank has contested the present petition ­ 3 ­ and filed the written statement in which it has been submitted that in exercise of powers conferred under sub section (4) of Section 45 of the Banking Regulation Act 1949, Reserve Bank of India prepared a scheme for amalgamation of the Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd.

with Canara Bank and the said scheme sanctioned by the Central Government under Section 45 (7) of the said Act and was notified in the gazette of India dated 23.08.1985 and the said amalgamation is not a transfer of tenancy and does not amount to an act of sub­letting, assignment or parting with the premises and therefore present petition is not maintainable on the ground of sub­letting u/s 14 (1) (b) of DRC Act and is liable to be dismissed.
It has been contended that petitioner has thorough knowledge that the premises in suit has been continuously in occupation of the respondent since the amalgamation of M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd.

with Canara Bank as the petitioner has been continuously residing in the same locality/area where the premises in suit is situated and the petitioner and her representative have been regularly visiting the premises in suit and have never raised any objection to the premises being occupied by the respondent as a tenant.

It has been submitted that the respondent bank has been in exclusive possession of tenanted premises since last 22 years in its own capacity and therefore there has been a implied consent of the landlord/petitioner for creation of tenancy in favour of the respondent. It is further contended that the petitioner was maintaining a saving account along with Mst. Atiya Rehman in their joint names with the respondent bank at Chandni Chowk Branch and the rent @ Rs.

240/­ per month has been credited in to the said Saving Account of the petitioner and the said rent was withdrawn from time to time by the petitioner and as such by her ­ 4 ­ conduct , the petitioner had impliedly accepted the respondent as her tenant and it cannot be alleged at this stage after the gap of 22 years by the landlord/ petitioner that the respondent bank is a sub­tenant in the tenanted premises.

It has been further contended that there is no cause of action on the ground u/s 14 (1) (f) of DRC Act and it has been submitted that the tenanted premises are being used as a godown by the respondent bank which is opened regularly by the bank officials and the same do not require any substantial repairs and are not in a dangerous condition and moreover no such document has been filed by the petitioner to show that she had applied to Local Authority for getting the Plans sanctioned or that the Local Authority had issued any notice to the petitioner to carry out repairs on account of unsafe condition of the premises or that she has necessary funds for reconstruction.

It has been further contended that present eviction petition filed by the petitioner is time barred as the petitioner/landlord did not take any action for years against the respondent bank and therefore the tenancy rights accrued in favour of the respondent. It has been further contended that the petitioner only wants to evict the respondent as she wants to let out the tenanted premise at a higher price and the respondent being the old tenant is an hurdle for the same.
The respondent has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
4. The petitioner has filed the replication in which the averments made in the petition are reiterated and the averments made in the written statement are stated to be wrong and controverted.

5. In order to prove her case the petitioner has examined ­ 5 ­ herself as PW­1 and evidence by way of affidavit has been filed as Ex. P­1 in which she has reiterated the averments made in the petition. She has placed on record the site plan as Ex. PW­1/1, the newspaper clipping alognwith its translation as Ex. PW­1/2 (Colly) and certified copy of permission from Competent Authority (Slum) as Ex. PW­1/3.

6. On the other hand, the respondent bank has examined Sh. R.K. Gupta, Sr. Manager, Canara Bank as RW­1 and evidence by way of affidavit has been filed as Ex.R1/A in which averments made in the written statement has been reiterated. He has placed on record the Notification of Government of India dated 23.08.1985 published in Gazette of India as Ex. RW­1/1, certified copy of the Statement of Account of saving account of the petitioner as Ex.
RW­1/2 (Colly) and letter dated 13.05.04 by the petitioner to the respondent bank with regard to change of her address as Ex. RW­1/3 and Ex. RW­1/4.
7. I have heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record carefully.

8. Ground U/s 14(1)(b) of DRC Act 14 (1) (b) of DRC Act reads as under:­ That the tenant has on or after the 9th day of 1952 sub let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord.

9. The Ld, Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner had let out the suit premises to M/s Lakshmi ­ 6 ­ Commercial Bank Ltd. and M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd. is claimed to have been merged and taken over by the respondent and as such M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd. ceased to exist and this merger/acquisition has been done without the consent of the petitioner and therefore it amounts to subletting, assigning or parting with the possession of the suit premises. The Ld.

Counsel for the petitioner has relied upon in support of his contentions the authorities titled as Parasam H. Rao Vs. Shantiprassad N. Kumar 1980 RLR SC 747, Cox & Kings Ltd. Vs. Chander Malhotra 1997 RLR 116 (SC), South Asia Industries Pvt. Ltd. Vs. S. Anup Singh and Singer India Ltd., Appellant Vs. Chander Mohan Chadha & Ors , Respondents AIR 2004 SC 4368.

10. On the other hand the Ld. Counsel for the respondent has vehemently argued that under the scheme of amalgamation u/s (4) of Section 45 of Banking Regulation Act 1949, RBI prepared a scheme for amalgamation of M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd. with the Canara Bank which was sanctioned by the Central Government and the same was notified in the Gazette of India dated 23.08.1985 and as such M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd.

merged with the Canara Bank under the legislative scheme and therefore it does not amount to subletting, assigning or parting with the possession of the suit premises. Ld. Counsel for the respondent has vehemently contended that the respondent is not sub tenant under the petitioner as the M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd.

was merged with the Canara Bank in the year 1985 and the present petition has been filed after a gap of 22 years and moreover, the respondent bank has been paying the rent all along to the petitioner and the petitioner was also maintaining a saving ­ 7 ­ account with the Canara Bank since 1988. She has further argued that the petitioner knows that the respondent bank has taken over M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd.

and the respondent bank is also remitting the rentals in the account of the petitioner and petitioner has not raised any objections for the last 22 years and therefore by virtue of acquiescence, the respondent has become the tenant as the petitioner has by her conduct accepted the respondent as a tenant. The Ld.

Counsel for the respondent has also argued that by virtue of aforesaid merger, all the assets and liabilities including the lease agreement, movable and immovable properties were taken over by the Canara Bank . In support of her contention, the Ld. Counsel for the respondent has relied upon in an authority titled as "Mrs. Asha Rohtagi & Ors. Vs Erstwhile New Bank of India through General Manager PNB". On the other hand, Ld.

Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the authority relied upon by the Ld. Counsel for the respondent is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case as the management of M/s Lakshmi Commercial Bank Ltd. which was the tenant of the petitioner and the management of the Canara Bank are entirely different and in the authority relied upon by Ld. Counsel for the respondent, both the banks were Nationalised bank.
